title: Osmosis and Water Potential Simulator
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Biology
description: Interactive MicroSim that visualizes how solute potential, pressure potential, temperature, and tonicity drive osmotic water movement.

learningObjectives: Calculate solute potential (Ψs) for internal and external solutions using Ψs = −iCRT.
Predict the direction of net water movement by comparing Ψcell and Ψexternal values.
Explain how hypotonic, isotonic, and hypertonic environments affect animal and plant cells differently.
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with diffusion and osmosis terminology
Ability to convert between degrees Celsius and Kelvin

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Interactive parameter exploration with staged conceptual feedback
keyQuestions: How does changing temperature alter Ψs values for the same concentrations?
Which side has the higher water potential and why?
What structural features allow plant cells to resist lysis during hypotonic stress?
commonMisconceptions: Water always moves toward the higher solute concentration regardless of pressure.
Plant and animal cells respond identically to hypertonic environments.
Temperature has no effect on osmotic movement.
assessmentOpportunities: Have students tune the sliders to achieve ΔΨ ≈ 0 MPa and explain their reasoning.
Ask learners to create a scenario that triggers the lysis warning and describe the underlying physics.
